ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
When Cosme correctly wears his new shirt, as shown on the left figure, the horizontal stripes form seven closed arches around his body. This morning he buttoned his shirt in the wrong way, as shown on the right. How many open arches were there around Cosme's body this morning?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: When Cosme correctly wears his new shirt, as shown on the left figure, the horizontal stripes form seven closed arches around his body. This morning he buttoned his shirt in the wrong way, as shown on the right. How many open arches were there around Cosme's body this morning?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the left figure, the shirt is buttoned normally, and the horizontal stripes on the two sides of the front placket meet at the same height, looking as if each horizontal stripe can form a closed ring-shaped arch around the body. In the right figure, the shirt is buttoned wrong by one position, the two sides of the front placket are vertically misaligned, and the endpoints of the horizontal stripes no longer connect with the endpoints of the original same horizontal stripe, but connect with the endpoints of a stripe at an adjacent height. Reasoning: The problem states that when worn correctly there are seven closed arches in total. If each closed arch is cut open at the shirt opening and viewed, the normal buttoning method is that the 1st stripe connects back to the 1st stripe, the 2nd stripe connects back to the 2nd stripe, and so on. After being buttoned wrong by one position, the connection relationship becomes the 1st stripe connecting to the 2nd stripe, the 2nd stripe connecting to the 3rd stripe, and so on all the way to the 7th stripe; in this way, the seven originally separate closed arches are joined into one continuous open arch, leaving only the top end and bottom end not closed. Therefore the number of open arches is 1.

method.method_draft: Model the stripes as connected curves cut at the shirt opening. First inspect the image: in the left shirt the stripe ends on the two front panels meet at the same heights, so each stripe is a separate closed arch around the body. In the right shirt, the buttons are fastened one position off, so the stripe end on one side of the opening lines up with the neighboring stripe end on the other side rather than its original mate. Use the text statement that there are seven closed arches when worn correctly. Under a one-level offset, the seven separate closed arches are spliced into one continuous chain: stripe 1 connects to stripe 2, stripe 2 to stripe 3, and so on, leaving only the two extreme ends unpaired. Therefore all seven become a single open arch, so the answer is 1.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：左图中，衬衫正常扣好，前襟两侧的水平条纹在同一高度相遇，看起来每一条横纹都能绕身体形成一个闭合的环状拱。右图中，衬衫扣错了一格，前襟两侧上下错位，横纹的端点不再与原来同一条横纹的端点相接，而是与相邻高度的横纹端点相接。推理：题目说明正确穿时共有七个闭合拱。把每个闭合拱在衬衫开口处切开来看，正常扣法是第1条接回第1条、第2条接回第2条，依此类推。错扣一格后，连接关系变成第1条接第2条、第2条接第3条，依此一直串到第7条；这样七个原本分开的闭合拱被拼成一条连续的开放拱，只剩最上端和最下端没有闭合。因此开放拱的数量是1。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This uses a topological/graph connection model of stripe endpoints rather than simply counting visible stripe segments. It tracks how wrong buttoning changes the pairing of the stripe ends.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the left figure as showing aligned stripe ends under correct buttoning, and the right figure as showing a one-button vertical offset where stripe ends meet adjacent levels across the front opening.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the statement that the correctly worn shirt has seven closed arches and that the right figure shows the wrongly buttoned state whose number of open arches is requested.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Key rule: if several closed loops are cut at the same opening and then reconnected with a one-step offset, the loops join into one continuous open chain with two unpaired ends.
